newsitem.title: USA: Early 1997 gold demand highest since 1993 - WGC.
newsitem.headline: Early 1997 gold demand highest since 1993 - WGC.

text.p: World demand for gold in the first quarter 1997 is running at its highest levels since 1993, New York based manager of market analysis for the World Gold Council, George Milling Stanley, said Friday.

"In addition, anecdotally we know Swiss gold refineries are running at full capacity and flights to transport gold in and out of Switzerland are apparently running up against prudential weight limits imposed by insurance companies," Milling-Stanley told a briefing on South Africa's mining industry hosted by the South African embassy in New York.

The World Gold Council (WGC) estimated first quarter 1993 gold demand in both developing and developed markets at 693.8 tonnes, after the spot gold price had fallen to around $350 an ounce in late 1991 from over just over $500 in late 1987.
Total world gold demand in the first quarter 1996 was estimated at 543.9, when the gold price rose to a five year high around $417 an ounce.
However, in the past year gold prices have since fallen back to three year lows around $336 in January 1997, before recovering to around $353 Friday.

In the long run the elasticity of gold demand with respect to a movement in gold prices is seen relatively low, other analysts said, but in the short run gold demand may be relatively sensitive to price movements, other analysts said.
"Sensitivity to price is greater in the Far East than in the US though," said Jeffrey Christian, managing director of New York based industry consultants, CPM Group.
"When the spot gold price dips below $360 an ounce, US jewellery manufacturers may produce heavier gold jewellery for the price, but retail margins mask the movement in the underlying price."

Gold imports by Dubai, an entrepot center for gold distribution to India, the world's largest consuming country, rose to a record 46 tonnes in January 1997, from 24 tonnes last year, Milling-Stanley said.
"Flights from Dubai to Calicott in India are also reported to be up against weight limits," he said.
"This is the first time in 20 years we have heard such stories," he said.
Full year 1996 demand for gold in India rose six percent to over 500 tonnes for the first time ever, the WGC said in its quarterly gold demand update published last month.

"Further rises in gold demand in India this year are likely as the Indian government doubled the amount of gold non-resident Indians may bring into the country to 10 kilograms every six months from five kilograms previously, he said.
